title: Follow an event through delay, replay, and dependency failure
description: Switch scenarios to see which paths remain authoritative, where state is protected, and what the product observes.

nodes.label: Event producer
nodes.detail: Creates a stable event ID, event timestamp, schema version, and source metadata before publishing.

nodes.label: Durable event log
nodes.detail: Orders events within a partition, retains them for replay, and applies bounded producer and consumer backpressure.

nodes.label: Stream processor
nodes.detail: Validates schemas, assigns watermarks, updates windows, joins state, and emits idempotent results.

nodes.label: Checkpointed state
nodes.detail: Stores window, join, and deduplication state together with the input positions required for consistent recovery.

nodes.label: Online feature store
nodes.detail: Publishes versioned, timestamped features for low-latency readers without becoming the source of raw event truth.

nodes.label: Model service
nodes.detail: Scores fresh features under a bounded deadline and returns an explicit degraded or unavailable state on failure.

nodes.label: Analytical sink
nodes.detail: Stores append-only events and corrected aggregates for reporting, backfills, evaluation, and investigation.

nodes.label: Decision consumer
nodes.detail: Applies idempotent actions and records the prediction, exposure, fallback, and eventual outcome join key.

scenarios.label: Fresh event
scenarios.summary: An on-time event updates checkpointed state, online features, the analytical history, and a model-backed decision.
scenarios.result: The decision uses a fresh feature version, while the durable log and checkpoint preserve replayability.

scenarios.label: Late event
scenarios.summary: The processor accepts an event behind the watermark only when the allowed-lateness policy permits a correction.
scenarios.result: Historical aggregates and future features are corrected; already-issued decisions remain traceable to their earlier feature version.

scenarios.label: Processor restart
scenarios.summary: The event log retains input while a replacement processor restores state and resumes from the matching checkpoint position.
scenarios.result: Freshness is temporarily degraded, but replay plus idempotent sinks prevents lost or duplicated business effects.

scenarios.label: Model outage
scenarios.summary: Streaming features and historical analytics remain healthy while synchronous model scoring is unavailable.
scenarios.result: The consumer uses a documented feature-based fallback or abstains; events continue so recovery does not require a data backfill.

scenarios.label: Analytics outage
scenarios.summary: The historical sink is unavailable, but the online feature and model path remains isolated from reporting.
scenarios.result: Online decisions continue; retained log data is replayed into the analytical sink after it recovers.
